premerge_pr.title: bench: prepare frozen one-core i9 diagnostic for #361
premerge_pr.body:
Prepare the frozen #361 versus v0.2.9 one-thread Wikidata diagnostic with the unchanged release-scaling driver. The previously failing allocation accounting now incorporates the exact independently reviewed #368 repair as appended commits, preserving #366 history and all failed evidence.

Current head: `d61e0976b6faa8e8b1dfdcb0e10bffdc28235108`. Reviewed commits map to appended `3b4350bb88944d50fe0dd2f9f99d466952b1ad10` and `4e671215051d5f5f9720c7bfa1944912b83643a2`; stable patch IDs match, and all 41 repair files byte-match `bfd5d322651974f9803f4c03942cf3ba3b5161d2`. No accounting-model change or new independent safety certification.

Frozen candidate `d33787e138426cb441db6975f54b2eccca02e89a`, baseline `b65b2aa54488f072cf005b8fe62461c32e6ef083`, ten paired Wikidata 1t rounds, original baseline/candidate ratio rule and driver SHA256 `6167171b7889706226340adc0beba89bfbf5e933af944d7f68e49d97bc7bfa07` remain unchanged. #361's adverse CI result and prior recorded tradeoffs stand.

Local untimed validation: four recipe tests passed with `ONECORE_REQUIRE_JUST=1`, zero skips, using real Just 1.38.0. Direct and root Just dry runs resolve the exact frozen commands. Driver/source correspondence, fetch-failure propagation, Rust formatting, Python syntax and whitespace checks pass. No local measurement ran.

[Append-only handoff and exact evidence](docs/journal/2026-11-12-onecore-preparation/HANDOFF.md). Completes implementation scope dispatched in #363/6810684246; changed-head CI/legacy observations are recorded separately in the completion REVIEW/state to avoid restarting CI with documentation pushes.

**Not workstation-ready:** applicable exact-head Actions/legacy, Coordinator reconciliation, separate deliberate master integration and PROTOCOL9 readiness remain required. No merge, queue entry, tag, Run signal, benchmark execution or default change is authorised by this delivery. The matched production/research inversion and whole-decoder context diagnostic from #372 remains a separate subsequent assignment.
